summary: SSO re-auth loop caused by IdP state param query normalization in private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightLens reports that after configuring Redwood Private SSO with their IdP, users attempting to sign in to the Redwood Console enter an endless redirect loop between /oauth2/authorize and the IdP; session is never established. Loop starts immediately after first successful redirect back to the console and affects all users in the tenant.

Impact:
- All BrightLens users unable to sign in to Redwood Console in production (us-west-2).
- Blocks admin operations and onboarding for new team members.
- No tokens are issued; API usage remains unaffected for pre-existing service accounts.

Environment:
- Redwood Private deployed to BrightLens VPC (customer-managed ingress).
- IdP: Okta hosted tenant (SAML->OIDC proxy for Redwood flows).
- Console: private console behind NGINX ingress provided by customer.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Browse to https://console.brightlens.internal/ and click "Sign in".
2) Console redirects to Redwood IdP proxy /oauth2/authorize with state=<base64url>.
3) IdP performs auth and redirects back to https://console.brightlens.internal/oauth2/callback?state=<same-value>&code=...
4) Ingress normalizes query and strips trailing '=' padding from state parameter (observed when proxy annotation `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/normalize-query: "true"` is set).
5) IdP proxy validates state and fails HMAC/state match -> treats callback as invalid state and issues a redirect to /oauth2/authorize, starting loop.

Expected behavior:
- Redirect callback should validate state and exchange code for tokens; user receives session cookie and lands on console.

Actual behavior:
- IdP callback fails state validation due to modified state param; no token exchange occurs and the user is sent back to the IdP. Repeats indefinitely until user cancels.

Observed logs and errors:
- idp-proxy logs (sample):
  "WARN auth: state validation failed: mismatch (expected HMAC=... got raw=...)"
  "INFO auth: initiating redirect to /oauth2/authorize (reason=invalid_state)"
- NGINX ingress logs show 302 chain where the state query value in incoming request is missing trailing '=' characters compared to outgoing redirect.
- Browser network trace: initial redirect URI contains state=eyJ0eXAi..., callback contains state=eyJ0eXAi... (truncated padding)

Timeline:
- 2025-02-10 09:12 PST: Customer opens support ticket reporting sign-in loop.
- 2025-02-10 09:25 PST: Triage by Support; assigned to Ethan (Auth on-call).
- 2025-02-10 10:05 PST: Reproduced in customer environment via support session.
- 2025-02-10 13:40 PST: Engineering engaged; hypothesis drafted.

Workarounds tried by customer before engagement:
- Redeploying ingress without normalize-query: no change (they had multiple ingress controllers, one of which still normalized).
- Enabling IdP fallback cookie: not configured.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced a minimal flow against a test console behind an NGINX ingress configured with `normalize-query: "true"`. When state was produced by our idp-proxy using standard base64url with padding, NGINX removed padding ("=") characters during normalization.
- Our state HMAC uses the exact serialized value; removing padding changes HMAC input causing mismatch.
- Customer's ingress has a managed annotation that normalizes query strings across their fleet; changes cannot be rolled back without coordination with their infra team.
- Confirmed that other customers using default ingress behavior are unaffected.

Hypothesis:
- Ingress query normalization is incompatible with our current state encoding (base64url with padding). The idp-proxy should either: 1) use a padding-insensitive state encoding, or 2) fall back to a cookie-based state store when callback state is missing/padding altered.

Next steps (plan):
- Short-term: implement cookie-based fallback in idp-proxy so that if state param validation fails but a signed cookie exists, we accept it and proceed (hotfix path).
- Short-term workaround for customer: add ingress annotation `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-preserve-query: "true"` and disable normalize-query, coordinate with customer infra to ensure all ingress controllers have same config.
- Medium-term: change state generation in idp-proxy to use URL-safe base64 WITHOUT padding and update validation to be tolerant of omission of padding characters.

Resolution summary:
- Deployed a targeted hotfix to idp-proxy (github.com/redwood/inference-idp-proxy PR #612): added a signed cookie fallback for state and improved base64url decoding to accept missing padding.
- Customer applied ingress annotation proxy-preserve-query: "true" across their ingress fleet (coordinated with their infra team).
- Verified end-to-end login: users complete auth and receive session cookie.
- Changes rolled out to BrightLens production at 2025-02-12 21:05 PST.

Follow-up actions / Postmortem items:
- [EN-447] Update idp-proxy to consistently emit paddingless base64url state and HMAC canonicalization across versions.
- [SUP-298742] Communicate recommended ingress annotations and a pre-deployment checklist for customers running private ingress controllers.
- Add an observable metric / alert for repeated invalid_state cycles per tenant.
comments: Priya Shah (Support) 2025-02-10: Customer reports console sign-in redirect loop; attaching screenshots and network HAR. Asked for environment details and recent changes.

BrightLens-Infra (Customer) 2025-02-10: Confirmed we recently upgraded our helm chart which toggled normalize-query on one of the ingress controllers. We can coord to change, but we'd prefer a server-side workaround if possible.
Ethan Cole (Auth on-call) 2025-02-10: Reproduced locally with ngnix test harness. Observed state padding being removed. Escalating to Eng (assigning to Diego for hotfix).
Diego Ramirez (Eng) 2025-02-10: Drafted hotfix: add cookie fallback and tolerant base64 decoding. Opening PR 612 for idp-proxy. Will run canary in staging and then customer prod after signoff.
BrightLens-SRE 2025-02-11: We applied proxy-preserve-query on one ingress and can confirm the loop stopped for that controller. We'll schedule the change across all ingress controllers tonight.
Ethan Cole 2025-02-12: Hotfix PR merged and built (image tag idp-proxy:release-2025-02-12-hotfix). Coordinated cutover window with customer at 21:00 PST.
Priya Shah 2025-02-12: Customer confirmed sign-in working post-deploy. Closing loop and documenting recommended ingress annotations in onboarding doc.
investigation_notes: Key finding: query normalization stripped padding '=' from base64url-encoded state, causing HMAC mismatch. Solution combined ingress config fix and idp-proxy server-side toleration (cookie fallback + padding-tolerant decode).
resolution_notes: Hotfix deployed to idp-proxy (PR #612). Customer applied ingress annotation to preserve query. Verified successful logins and monitored for 24 hours. Recommended follow-ups added to backlog.
public_resolution_summary: Root cause: customer's ingress normalized query strings and removed padding characters from the OAuth 'state' param which caused our IdP proxy to reject the callback. We deployed a hotfix to accept missing padding and added a cookie-based fallback for state, and customer updated ingress annotations. Login functionality restored.
